mathematical_review.map_direction: The braid-to-mapping-class isomorphism is Ψ:G_n→Mod(D²,Q_n;∂D²). The endpoint homomorphism is π_geo:G_n→S_n. The diagram should draw Ψ from geometric braids to boundary-fixed mapping classes; the conclusion restricts this same forward map to ker(π_geo).
mathematical_review.commuting_permutation_square: The proof establishes that the permutation of Q_n induced by Ψ([β]) is exactly π_geo([β]): the lifted homeomorphism endpoint h_β satisfies h_β(q_j)=z_j(1)=q_(π_geo([β])(j)). Thus the square with π_geo on G_n and the induced marked-point permutation on Mod commutes with identity on S_n. The tuple endpoint record here is π_geo([β]), not its inverse; the inverse in covering monodromy is a separate label-versus-action convention noted in the remarks.
mathematical_review.kernel_and_purity: G_n^pure is ker(π_geo). PMod(D²,Q_n;∂D²) consists of classes inducing the identity permutation on Q_n, within Mod(D²,Q_n;∂D²). Commutativity and bijectivity of Ψ imply Ψ(ker π_geo)=PMod; the restricted map is an isomorphism onto that subgroup.
mathematical_review.boundary_and_punctures: The target mapping classes fix ∂D² pointwise and preserve Q_n setwise; purity strengthens this to fixing each marked point. Any schematic should retain the boundary-fixed qualifier and distinguish setwise puncture preservation in Mod from pointwise preservation in PMod.
mathematical_review.small_cases_and_conventions: The statement includes n≥0, with n≤1 trivial. No particular braid word, crossing sequence, or alternative product order is needed for this kernel-identification diagram.

diagram_recommendation.content: Draw the commuting square G_n --Ψ--> Mod(D²,Q_n;∂D²), with vertical endpoint-permutation maps π_geo and π_Q to S_n and identity on S_n. Then mark the kernels and show the restricted horizontal isomorphism ker(π_geo)=G_n^pure --Ψ|--> PMod(D²,Q_n;∂D²), the pointwise-puncture stabilizer inside the boundary-fixed, setwise-puncture-preserving mapping class group. Label Ψ in the forward braid-to-mapping-class direction; preserve pointwise boundary fixing, setwise versus pointwise puncture conditions, and the equality of the two permutation maps. Do not insert an inverse on the top-row endpoint permutation; the inverse monodromy convention is a different map.
